plan.brief:
Are our CI jobs taking more time? Because we have to optimize it we have to make it under 2 minutes. for the whole sofar.

Operator rulings (2026-11-16): "Run what a change touches (Recommended)" — record-only pushes run only the record checks, TypeScript changes run a split vitest suite, Rust changes run the Rust matrix, and workflow edits, PRs and tags run everything. "Every push, made faster (Recommended)" — all 5 platforms stay on Rust pushes; Intel Mac moves to an arm runner under Rosetta.
plan.goal: Every push to sofar's CI finishes in under 2 minutes of wall clock, measured from push to the last job's end on a warm cache. CI runs only what a change touches. Every PR into main and every release tag run everything. All 5 Rust platforms stay on Rust pushes, made faster.

tasks.title: A `changes` job classifies each push or PR by path (record, ts, rust, ffi, workflow). Every other job gates on it; workflow edits and PRs and tags run everything.
Drop the unused release build and artifact upload from the push core job; release.yml builds its own cores (r4-fixes M16)
Fold the js_log crosscheck into the one cargo test invocation, so its 30–169s second pass goes
Split the vitest unit suite across parallel runners per Node version (vitest --shard)
Shard parity:real (213–298s) and real-logs across runners by record
Intel Mac: cross-build x86_64-apple-darwin on the arm runner and run its tests under Rosetta
apple job: test the host slice on push; the full 4-slice xcframework only on PRs and tags
Measure the wall clock per change class (record-only, TypeScript, Rust, workflow) on warm caches; every class is under 120s or the gap is logged with its cause

payload.summary:
The operator asked that sofar's CI stay under 2 minutes. Warm-cache runs took about 10 minutes; cold runs up to 18. The biggest costs were:
- parity:real, 213–298s on 2 jobs.
- The vitest suite, 204–319s on one runner.
- The push-path release build with fat LTO, which is unused, at 65–254s.
- The Intel Mac runner, 441–1042s.
- A recompile in the js_log step, because it used a different package set.
- Two thirds of pushes are record-only but ran everything.

Changes:
- `ci.yml` is restructured. A `changes` job classifies each push by path. Vitest runs as 4 shards per Node version. parity-real runs as 8 shards dealt by log size. Conformance, real-logs and render each have their own job and build a `ci`-profile core without LTO.
- Intel Mac cross-builds on the arm runner and runs its tests under Rosetta.
- On a push the apple job builds only the macOS host slice, without LTO.
- Release artifacts are built only on dispatch.

Verified locally: the `ci`-profile core passes conformance (67) and fold-parity plus real-logs (431); 8 parity shards cover all 78 records once (44s wall); vitest shard 1/4 passes in 30s; `build-apple.sh --test --host` passes. Nothing has run on GitHub yet.
